clue.text: German sectarian in school, reverse of learned, following senior

parts.note: SCH is a standard abbreviation for school

indicators.note: the reverse of a word is that word written from its last letter back to its first

parts.note: learned in the sense of came to know
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
an elder is one's senior

explanation.surface: A German religious dissenter is placed somewhere in a school's hierarchy below a senior.
explanation.walkthrough: SCH + WENK (KNEW backwards) + F + ELDER. The Schwenkfelders followed Kaspar Schwenkfeld, a 16th-century Silesian reformer.
explanation.definitionFit: A Schwenkfelder is a member of the Protestant sect founded by the German reformer Schwenkfeld.

clue.text: Meat coated in salt — it's hot and dry

definitions.note: a description of the thing, standing for a noun

indicators.note: something coated in another is wrapped inside it

parts.note: sal is the chemist's Latin word for salt
ham is a meat

explanation.surface: Salted meat, hot and dry, as in a cured ham.
explanation.walkthrough: Sal is Latin for salt, familiar from chemistry names like sal volatile.
explanation.definitionFit: The shamal is a hot, dry northwesterly wind blowing across Iraq and the Persian Gulf.

clue.text: Company deficit is not special — these are huge

indicators.note: not tells us a letter is taken away from the word before it

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
a deficit is a loss
taken as written
S is an abbreviation for special

explanation.surface: A firm's shortfall is unremarkable, though some debts are enormous.
explanation.walkthrough: IS without S leaves I: CO + LOSS + I.
explanation.definitionFit: Colossi, plural of colossus, are gigantic statues or things of enormous size.

clue.text: ——, it's time to relax — does it involve getting hammered?

definitions.note: the blank stands for the answer, completing the sentence: work is over
definitions.meaning: first meaning: read as '...', the working day finished
second meaning: a beating, in which the victim is hammered

explanation.walkthrough: Fill the blank with the answer and the first half says the day's work is done; 'hammered' also hints at getting drunk once relaxing, but the sense is being beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: A working-over is slang for a severe beating, and read as two words it says work has ended.

clue.text: Guinness from the brewery needed for impatient Irelanders?

indicators.note: the letters needed are found within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Fresh Guinness from the brewery is wanted by thirsty Irish drinkers.
explanation.walkthrough: Entire is an old term for porter or stout drawn direct from the brewery, of which Guinness is the famous Irish example.
explanation.definitionFit: Entire was a name for porter, the dark beer brewers sent out ready-mixed, as Guinness stout is.

clue.text: Jock's personal Parisian manikin

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Scots for own; Jock is a nickname for a Scot
second meaning: the French word for a dwarf

explanation.walkthrough: Jock signals a Scots word and Parisian a French one; the same four letters serve both.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots nain means own or personal, and French nain means a dwarf, which a manikin is.

clue.text: Arm (fin) to cover 'fair warrior'

parts.note: fin is slang for an arm or hand, as the bracket confirms
to lay is to cover, as with a cloth

explanation.surface: An arm is armour for a fair warrior, as a fin is for a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: FIN + LAY. Finlay is a Scottish given name, said to come from Gaelic Fionnlagh, meaning fair warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: The name Finlay derives from Gaelic words translated as fair warrior, so the meaning stands for the name.

clue.text: Clumsy fellow near, my set's cracked — it can lead to leaks (11, two words)

parts.note: a lob is a lout or clumsy person

indicators.note: something cracked is broken up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: by means near
taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A clumsy man breaks someone's set nearby, which leads to things leaking.
explanation.walkthrough: The lobby system is the arrangement giving accredited journalists off-the-record briefings at Westminster, a source of political leaks.
explanation.definitionFit: The parliamentary lobby system briefs journalists unattributably, so it is a classic channel for leaked information.

clue.text: Doctor uniquely curtailed on type of fibre

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
uniquely, as in solely, means alone

explanation.surface: A doctor gives a unique, short lecture on some type of fibre.
explanation.walkthrough: DR + ALONE without its final E.
explanation.definitionFit: Dralon is a trademarked acrylic fibre used for upholstery and furnishing fabrics.

clue.text: His life's carefree. Alpine, perhaps

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the man in the phrase 'the life of ...', an easy existence
second meaning: a make of car, of which the Alpine tourer was a model

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a carefree alpine holiday; Alpine is a model of the old British Riley car.
explanation.definitionFit: Living the life of Riley is an idiom for luxurious ease, and Riley was a British car maker with an Alpine model.

clue.text: Type of flagellate from domain that's obscure

indicators.note: something obscure is muddled and unclear, so the letters before it are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Some kind of flagellate organism comes from an obscure scientific domain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' looks like a link word between definition and wordplay, but it belongs to the letters being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Monadiform means shaped like a monad, a tiny single-celled flagellate organism, so it names a form of flagellate.

clue.text: Veg diet is varied for processing food

indicators.note: something varied has been altered, so the letters before it change order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A vegetable diet is changed to suit food processing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' does double service in the surface as a verb but here supplies two letters of the rearranged material.
explanation.definitionFit: Digestive describes what serves digestion, the body's breaking down of food.

clue.text: What's central to change is moving to end emergency?

definitions.note: a definition by example: an alert is issued in an emergency

indicators.note: the letter taken out is moved along to sit after the rest of the word
the central letter of the word that follows is picked out and taken from its place

parts.note: to change is to alter

explanation.surface: A question about what lies at the heart of changing an emergency.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of ALTER, a T, goes to the end: AL + ER + T gives ALERT.
explanation.definitionFit: An alert is a warning state declared when danger looms, which is the situation of an emergency, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Extra noggin set before the assembled company

indicators.note: one piece is placed ahead of the other in the answer

parts.note: nob and noggin are both slang for the head
everyone gathered is all

explanation.surface: An extra drink is poured before the gathered guests.
explanation.walkthrough: A noggin is also a small measure of drink, which the surface leans on. In cricket an extra is a run not scored off the bat, and a no-ball is one kind.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a no-ball, an illegal delivery, adds a run to the batting side's total as one of the extras.

clue.text: See ruler taken in by magic herb? How jester reacts!

indicators.note: something taken in by another is held inside it

parts.note: moly is the magic herb Hermes gave Odysseus against Circe
the letter C is said like the word see
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: A king falls under the spell of a magic herb, and the court fool's response is shown.
explanation.walkthrough: Moly is the herb Hermes gives Odysseus in Homer to resist Circe's magic; 'See' supplies a letter by sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A jester mocks; responding mockingly is how a court fool characteristically answers, an adverb for his manner.

clue.text: Nile low?

definitions.note: the word that names this Nile, not the river itself
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the ... Nile, one of the river's two main branches
second meaning: down in spirits, depressed

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a river running low; the answer instead names a branch of the Nile and a mood.
explanation.definitionFit: The Blue Nile is one of the two great tributaries, and feeling blue means being sad or dejected.

clue.text: Tower up, like dish with recipe for stuffing

parts.note: as means like

indicators.note: stuffing goes inside something, so this piece sits within the other

parts.note: a pie is a dish
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin, on prescriptions

explanation.surface: Instructions for building a towering pie with a stuffing recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: AS + PI(R)E. The sense of aspire is the older, literal one of rising high.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers gives aspire the literal sense of rising or towering upward, as a spire does.

clue.text: The old in retreat about say-so, uneasily indifferent

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the word is read in reverse
one piece goes about, that is around, the other

parts.note: ye is the old form of the

indicators.note: an uneasy arrangement is unsettled, so these letters are shaken up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Old people in a retirement home react uneasily and indifferently to someone's say-so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The old' here is the archaic spelling of the word 'the', not elderly people.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy-osy is a colloquial term for easygoing or casual, so someone easy-osy is indifferent to outcomes.

clue.text: Man noted for his song, unaccompanied, this writer's French

parts.note: solo means unaccompanied
this writer's means my, and the French is mon

explanation.surface: A man is known for singing alone in French.
explanation.walkthrough: The Song of Solomon, or Song of Songs, is a book of the Bible traditionally ascribed to King Solomon.
explanation.definitionFit: King Solomon is credited with the biblical Song of Solomon, so he is famous for his song.

clue.text: Core coat in aquatint images

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A central layer of paint appears in aquatint prints.
explanation.definitionFit: The intima is the innermost lining of an artery or vein, the coat nearest the core.

clue.text: Carriage pin found in old pot

indicators.note: something found in another sits inside it

parts.note: tea was old slang for marijuana, also called pot
pins is slang for legs

explanation.surface: A pin turns up in an old pot inside a carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: Pins is slang for legs, and in old slang tea meant marijuana, as pot does now.
explanation.definitionFit: A telega is a rough four-wheeled Russian cart, a horse-drawn carriage without springs.

clue.text: Early flight for holiday destination, often

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an obsolete word for a flight of steps
second meaning: a country popular with tourists

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a morning plane to the sun; the first meaning is archaic, a flight of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Greece, from Latin gradus, once meant a flight of steps, and the country Greece is a favourite holiday spot.

clue.text: Toil over painting e.g. eucalypt

parts.note: to tew is to toil or work hard
painting is an example of art; over places it after the toil

explanation.surface: Someone labours on a painting of a eucalyptus tree.
explanation.walkthrough: TEW + ART. The tewart is a Western Australian eucalyptus with very hard timber.
explanation.definitionFit: The tewart, or tuart, is a species of eucalyptus native to Western Australia.

clue.text: Fairy dance, right round the family fire?

indicators.note: one piece goes round the other, enclosing it

parts.note: RT is an abbreviation for right
an ingle is a fire on a domestic hearth

explanation.surface: A question about fairies dancing around the family's fireside.
explanation.walkthrough: An ingle is a fireside or hearth fire, as in inglenook.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringlet is an old term for a circular dance of fairies, the kind supposed to leave a fairy ring.

clue.text: River, rapid roller near battlefield, one in spate?

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river
the Iser rolls rapidly beside the battlefield of Hohenlinden in Campbell's poem

explanation.surface: A fast river near a battlefield bursts its banks.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Campbell's poem 'Hohenlinden' describes the Iser 'rolling rapidly' by the battle. A river in spate is rising.
explanation.definitionFit: A river in spate is in flood, its level rising, so it is a riser.

clue.text: What's dray delivered unusually, line not fashionable? (6, two words)

definitions.text: What's dray delivered unusually, line not fashionable?

indicators.note: something done unusually departs from the normal order, so the word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: not means the word after it is removed from the one before

parts.note: taken as written
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: A query about what a brewer's dray, delivering oddly, carries in an unfashionable brand.
explanation.walkthrough: DRAY rearranged, then LINE without IN. The whole clue doubles as the definition: dray horses traditionally delivered beer, here a dry ale.
explanation.definitionFit: A dray is a brewer's cart, and dry ale, a less sweet beer, is the sort of cargo it delivers.

clue.text: Keen on a selection of skin tones

indicators.note: a selection is a run of letters taken from the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Someone is fond of a range of skin tones, as in make-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Being into something is a colloquial way of saying one is enthusiastic about it.

clue.text: In which you might find we'd sit endlessly diverted with hols? (9, two words)

definitions.text: In which you might find we'd sit endlessly diverted with hols?

indicators.note: without its end, the last letter of the word is dropped
diverted means turned from the original course, so the letters take a new order

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored
the word without its last letter
taken as written; hols is British slang for holidays

explanation.surface: Where you sit, endlessly entertained or bored, by friends' holiday pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: guests sitting endlessly through someone's holiday photographs is the classic slide show. Hols is British for holidays.
explanation.definitionFit: A slide show projects photographs one after another, the traditional way of showing off holiday snaps to visitors.

clue.text: Ring of the bell? My hooter was lit, too

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the sound a bell makes
second meaning: Edward Lear's creature with the luminous nose, speaking for himself

explanation.walkthrough: Edward Lear's poem 'The Dong with a Luminous Nose' gives the second sense; hooter is slang for nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A dong is the deep sound of a bell, and Lear's Dong had a nose that glowed in the dark.

clue.text: Old Scotsman's deranged to compete at Klosters, one might suppose?

definitions.note: old Scots usage; the answer is an adjective

parts.note: Klosters is a Swiss ski resort, so ski is what you do there
to vie is to compete

explanation.surface: An old Scotsman would have to be mad to take part in a race at a Swiss resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to compete at Klosters' reads as ski + vie, a ski race; Klosters is a Swiss ski resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Skivie is an old Scots adjective meaning deranged or crazy, so the old Scotsman's word for deranged.

clue.text: Eat cored and mashed yam roots

indicators.note: with its core taken out, the middle letter is removed

parts.note: the word without its middle letter

indicators.note: mashed food is pulped into a new shape, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A kitchen instruction: eat cored and mashed yam roots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roots' looks like part of the recipe, the yams themselves, but it is the definition, in the sense of word origins.
explanation.definitionFit: Etyma is the plural of etymon, the original form from which a word derives, its linguistic root.

clue.text: Some work round Mid-East, odd scene for what debs go through?

indicators.note: one piece goes round, enclosing, the other

parts.note: the erg is a small unit of work in physics
ME is the abbreviation for Middle East

indicators.note: an odd version of a word is a strange one, its letters jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Describes a strange Middle Eastern party scene through which debutantes must pass.
explanation.walkthrough: Debutantes, or debs, make their first formal entry into society, their coming out, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A debutante's coming-out is her emergence into high society, so emergences are what debs undergo.

clue.text: Shuffle back row organized to catch circling chaps

indicators.note: circling something means going all round it, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: the rear is the back rank of an army
to run something is to organize it
to get is to catch
chaps are men

explanation.surface: A sports team rearranges its back row so it can pick off players running round.
explanation.walkthrough: REAR + RAN + GE(MEN)T. 'Shuffle' looks like an anagram signal but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A shuffle, as of cards or a cabinet, is a reordering, which is exactly what a rearrangement is.
